title: Commonitorium Primum [ex Editione Baluziana]
author: Vincentius Lirinensis

passages.original: Quia videlice Scripturam sacram pro ipsa sua altitudine non uno eodemque sensu universi accipiunt, sed ejusdem eloquia aliter atque aliter alius atque alius interpretatur; ut pene quot homines sunt, tot illinc sententiae erui posse videantur. Aliter namque illam Novatianus, aliter Sabellius, aliter Donatus exponit, aliter Arius, Eu- nomius, Macedonius; aliter Photinus, Apollinaris, Priscillianus, aliter Jovinianus, Pelagius , Caelestius; aliter postremo Nestorius. Atque idcirco multùm necesse est, propter tantos tam varii erroris anfractus, ut propheticae et apostolice interpretationis linea secundum Ecclesiastici et Catholici sensus normam dirigatur.
passages.english: Because, that is, owing to its very depth, not all people take sacred Scripture in one and the same sense, but one person interprets its words one way and another another, so that it seems possible to draw from it almost as many opinions as there are people. For Novatian expounds it one way, Sabellius another, Donatus another; Arius, Eunomius and Macedonius another; Photinus, Apollinaris and Priscillian another; Jovinian, Pelagius and Caelestius another; and lastly Nestorius another. And therefore, because of so many twists and turns of such varied error, it is very necessary that the line of prophetic and apostolic interpretation be directed according to the rule of the ecclesiastical and Catholic sense.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'videlice' read as 'videlicet', 'Eu- nomius' as 'Eunomius', 'apostolice' as 'apostolicae'.

passages.original: Sed et ejusdem Epistolæ testimonium perhibent quas ad Philippum Imperatorem (3), qui primus Romanorum Principum Christiaaus fuit, Christiani magisterii auctoritate conscripsi. De cujus incredibili quadam scientia si quis referentibus nobis Christianum non. accepit testimonium, saltem testificantibus philosophis gentilem recipiat confessionem. Ait namque impius ille Porphyrius (1) excitum se fama ipsius Alexandriam puerum fere perrexisse, ibique eum vidisse jam senem, sed plane talem tautumque qui arcem totius scientiæ condi- disset. Dies me citius defecerit quam ea quae in illo viro præclara exstiterunt vel ex minima saltem parte perstringam : quæ tamen omnia non solum ad Religionis gloriam, sed etiam ad tentationis magnitudinem pertinebant.
passages.english: But the letters of the same man also bear witness, which he wrote with the authority of a Christian teacher to the Emperor Philip, who was the first of the Roman princes to be a Christian. And if anyone does not accept the Christian testimony about his almost incredible learning when we report it, let him at least accept the confession of a pagan, with philosophers bearing witness. For that impious Porphyry says that, roused by his fame, he went to Alexandria when he was almost a boy, and there saw him, already an old man, but plainly such and so great a man as had built the citadel of all knowledge. Day would fail me sooner than I could touch on even the smallest part of the things that were outstanding in that man; yet all of them tended not only to the glory of religion but also to the greatness of the temptation.
passages.notes: The text has the edition's footnote markers (3) and (1), omitted. 'conscripsi' (first person, 'I wrote') must be a misreading or slip for 'conscripsit' ('he wrote'), since the letters are Origen's; translated as 'he wrote'. 'Christiaaus', 'tautumque' and 'condi- disset' are scanning errors for 'Christianus', 'tantumque' and 'condidisset'. The 'non.' has a stray period.

passages.original: Et tamen hic quoque post haec omnia, hic, inquam, Tertullia- nus, catholici dogmatis, id est, universalis ac vetustæ Mei parum tenax, ac disertior multo quam felicior, I mutata deinceps sententia, fecit ad extremum quod de eo beatus confessor Hilarius quodam loco scribit : Sequenti, inquit, errore detraxit scriptis probabilibus auctoritatem, Hilarius in Matth. c. 5. Et fuit ipse quoque in Ecclesia magna tentatio. Sed de hoc nolo plura dicere. Hoc tantum commemorabo, quod contra Moysi præceptum exsurgentes in Ecclesia novellasMontani furias et insana illa insanarum mulicrum novitii dogmatis somnia (1) veras prophetias adseverando, meruit ut de se quoque et scripturis suis diceretur: Si surrexerit in medio tuî propheta.
passages.english: And yet this man too, after all these things, this man, I say, Tertullian, holding too loosely to catholic doctrine, that is, to the universal and ancient faith, and far more eloquent than fortunate, afterwards changed his opinion and at last did what the blessed confessor Hilary writes of him in a certain place: "By his later error," he says, "he took away the authority from his approved writings" (Hilary, On Matthew, ch. 5). And he too was a great temptation in the Church. But I do not want to say more about him. I will mention only this: that by asserting, against the command of Moses, that the new frenzies of Montanus rising up in the Church, and those insane dreams of a newfangled doctrine of insane women, were true prophecies, he deserved to have it said of himself and his writings as well: "If a prophet arises in your midst."
passages.notes: 'Mei' is a scanning error for 'fidei' (faith); 'mulicrum' for 'mulierum'; 'I mutata' has a stray 'I'. The footnote marker (1) is omitted. The biblical quotation is from Deuteronomy 13 and continues after the passage. The words 'Hilarius in Matth. c. 5' appear to be a reference the edition inserted into the text.
